findings.title: Shared RunObserver state is pruned per project tick
A CUT_OFF tick can still launch all planned runs and reports the wrong result
findings.description: `_act()` checks `budget.allows_call()` only before each `Popen`, and `TickBudget` bounds when a call may *start*, not how long it runs (`src/amoeba/runner/budget.py:27-31`). A clock that crosses the deadline during the preceding poll/probe/store stages does not prevent a launch that was already planned: the first launch can start before the deadline, the next launch is refused and `CUT_OFF` returned, or — with one action — the tick launches it and then returns `COMPLETE` even though the deadline has passed. This contradicts the documented `CUT_OFF when the budget ran out` contract (`src/amoeba/runner/tick.py:88`) and the tick-level `test_a_cut_off_tick_closes_nothing` only covers a deadline of zero, where no calls happen at all. Check the budget at the stage boundary too (before deciding/acting), and add a test where the deadline expires after observation but before `_act()`.

findings.title: Store failures are swallowed by the runner's broad catch and converted into an escalation
findings.description: The re-raise tuple `STORE_FAILURES` (`src/amoeba/runner/faults.py:51-56`) covers only `StoreBusyError`, `StoreCorruptError`, `StorePermissionError`, `StoreSchemaError`, and `sqlite3.Error`. The store's own base class is `StoreError`, and it also raises `StoreIntegrityError`, `NodeNotFoundError`, `InvalidTransitionError`, and `UnknownVocabularyValueError` (`src/amoeba/store/models.py:139-190`). Those are caught by `except Exception`, logged, and passed to `escalate()`, which itself performs more store writes. A broken/corrupt/raced store is therefore reported as a per-project `unexpected_fault`, the process keeps running, and the escalation write can fail again. The docstring claims "a store failure ... re-raises and the process exits"; the tests only parametrize `StoreBusyError` and `UpstreamShapeError`. Re-raise `StoreError` (and preferably the whole typed store hierarchy) alongside `UpstreamShapeError`, and add a regression test for e.g. `StoreIntegrityError`.

findings.title: Escalation payloads can persist untrusted stderr tails verbatim
findings.description: `LaunchFailed.tail` comes from up to 4 KiB of the detached child's stderr (`src/amoeba/runner/launch.py:98-109`) or from `_still_overdue`'s fault detail (`src/amoeba/runner/observe.py:251-270`). `_record_launch_failed` puts that raw text into `context` and `PAYLOAD_STDERR_TAIL`, and `finish._block_once` → `Store.block()` → `_write_block()` stores it verbatim in the `blocked_states.context` and `messages.payload` columns. Those values are externally visible through `inspect` and the feed, yet `JournalEntry`'s own contract says "Callers must not place secrets in them" (`src/amoeba/store/journal_models.py:96-103`) and `ProjectEscalationOperations` repeats the warning. A provider that prints credentials to stderr therefore leaks them into durable, operator-visible records — including the environment that `launch()` deliberately says is never logged. Redact/bound secrets before persisting external output, or document and enforce a sanitization boundary with tests that inject credential-shaped stderr.

findings.title: `validate_settings` omits documented startup invariants
findings.description: `ProcessSettings` documents `tick_call_timeout_seconds` as "Larger than `tick_deadline_seconds` so one call that starts just inside the deadline still has room to finish" (`src/amoeba/process/settings.py:74-77`), and `--sq-timeout` as the bound on the Runner's `sq` probe. `validate_settings()` checks only three positivity constraints plus `tick_call_timeout < shutdown_grace`; it does not check `tick_call_timeout > tick_deadline`, `shutdown_grace > 0`, `sq_timeout > 0`, or `launch_grace >= 0`. Because `settings_flags.py` exposes all of these as `type=float` with no validation, `amoeba start --tick-deadline 10 --tick-call-timeout 1` boots successfully with a budget that contradicts the design, and a zero/negative `sq_timeout` makes the start-up probe time out. Validate the full documented invariant set at the factory boundary and parametrize tests for each violated relation.

findings.title: Runner's simulation/concurrency paths have no dedicated load test
findings.description: The Python rules require "any code on the simulation, network, concurrency, or environment-layer paths" to have at least one load test asserting latency/throughput/resource bounds, gated in CI. This change adds a resident-process tenant that performs per-tick subprocess polling, `cf` probes, detached `Popen` launches, and a `TickBudget` deadline, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already gates `pytest tests/load`. Yet `tests/load/` contains no runner or `TickBudget` test: the files are `test_cf_watch_load.py`, `test_crash_loop.py`, `test_feed_and_detection_load.py`, `test_harness_smoke.py`, `test_inbox_concurrent.py`, `test_recovery_scale.py`, `test_serve_load.py`, `test_verdict_concurrent.py`, and none reference `runner`, `Runner`, `TickBudget`, or `tick_deadline`. `tests/runner/test_budget_coverage.py` is a unit test with injected clocks, so it cannot detect event-loop starvation, per-tick latency growth with many projects/runs, or child-process resource leakage. Add a `tests/load/test_runner_load.py` that drives a realistic multi-project/many-run configuration through `RunnerTenant.tick` and asserts a per-tick bound plus no leaked `Popen` handles.

findings.title: New CLI harness injects a stub that breaks existing version-label assertions
findings.description: `cli_environment()` now prepends `write_sq_stub(...)` to `PATH` for every CLI test. The `sq` stub's generated script does not handle `sq --version`: it falls through to `mode = os.environ[MODE_ENV]` and, when `SQ_STUB_MODE` is unset (the default for the CLI harness), raises `KeyError` and exits non-zero. `capture_sq_version_label()` then records `VERSION_UNAVAILABLE` (`src/amoeba/process/version_label.py:34-38`) instead of the fake label. `tests/cli/test_detection_end_to_end.py:129-130` explicitly expects `FAKE_SQ_LABEL` from `DetectionE2E`'s own fake `sq`, but that fake is now shadowed by the stub placed in `cli_environment()` before `DetectionE2E.__init__` prepends `fake_bin`. Several other CLI tests that start the process also inherit a nonfunctional `sq --version`. Either teach the stub to answer `--version` (and set a stable label), or make `DetectionE2E` and other harnesses override `PATH` after composing `cli_environment()` so their fake wins; add an assertion that the start-up label is the expected one.

findings.title: Test helper imports a private helper from another test module
findings.description: `from runner.test_probes import _link  # pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]` reaches into another test module's private `_link()` helper. The same helper is defined anew in `tests/runner/test_probes.py:203-210`, so the link-submission recipe now has two homes and one test file has a static dependency on another test's collection/module. This is fragile under pytest's `-p`/parallel collection and violates the DRY/shared-fixture conventions. Move `_link()` into `tests/runner/tick_support.py` (or a shared `conftest.py` fixture) and import it from both test modules.

findings.title: Stale docstring contradicts the completed escalation implementation
findings.description: The module docstring still says "Escalation writes join this module in a later task." The same file now defines `raise_expected_faults()` (`line 120`) and `escalate()` (`line 152`), both of which perform escalation writes. This is misleading for maintainers reading the process-boundary contract. Remove the stale sentence and replace it with a one-line description of the two escalation paths (expected project-scoped fault vs unexpected node/project fault).
